propositions.text: Claimant is a Ukrainian citizen claiming refugee protection under sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX, a citizen of Ukraine, is claiming refugee protection under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (the Act).

propositions.text: Panel considered IRB Chairperson's guidelines on women refugee claimants fearing gender-related persecution.
propositions.quote: The panel has taken into account the IRB Chairperson's guidelines on Women Refugee Claimants Fearing Gender-Related Persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant is a Ukrainian citizen claiming refugee protection and the panel considered guidelines on women fearing gender-related persecution.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges she began a romantic relationship with her general manager in 2008 and was asked to sign papers to shift liability, which she refused due to suspicion of his ties to organized crime.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleged that in XXXX 2008, she began a romantic relationship with XXXX XXXX, the general manager of the XXXX for which she worked... She refused to sign these papers and told him that she was suspicious of his ties with these people.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges the manager slapped and insulted her after she refused to sign papers and asked him to leave her home.
propositions.quote: Angered, XXXX slapped and insulted her. The claimant then asked him to leave her home.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges a 2008 relationship with her manager who asked her to sign papers; she refused and was slapped and insulted.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges she was threatened by a man telling her to obey XXXX or be disfigured, and she reported this to police who doubted her account.
propositions.quote: On Monday, XXXX XXXX XXXX 2008, the claimant was heading to work when she was stopped by a car... He also told her to do everything XXXX told her to do and that if she did anything to the contrary, he would not kill her but would disfigure her... She went to the police to report these threats... the detective invited her into his office and asked her if she had noted the licence plate number... the owner of the car told them on the telephone that no one except him could have driven this vehicle.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges XXXX apologized and invited her to a restaurant where a man threatened them to remove XXXX's name from a list or face major problems, police would not intervene.
propositions.quote: At the end of the day, XXXX came to apologize... At about 10:00 p.m.,... the waiter came to tell XXXX that someone sitting farther in the restaurant wanted to speak with him... He told the claimant that this man was the owner of all the XXXX XXXX in the district... He asked him to remove his name from the list of XXXX, or else he and she would have major problems... He said that the police would never go after this important man.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges threats from a man to obey XXXX or be disfigured, police doubted her report; later a man threatened them at a restaurant to remove XXXX's name from a list.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges the director of XXXX was killed in a suspicious car accident, she was offered a trip to Budapest by XXXX, lost her job, and was kidnapped, beaten, and raped after reporting suspicions to police.
propositions.quote: A week later, the director of the XXXX XXXX, Mr. XXXX, was killed in a car accident... She went to XXXX's home; he calmed her down... She went there alone from XXXX XXXX to XXXX XXXX, 2008... When she returned, she found out that she had lost her job... She decided to write a letter to the prosecutor... On XXXX XXXX, 2008, she went to these offices... Two days later... she was kidnapped and taken to a house... She was beaten and raped... She managed to remove it, and she escaped.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges the director died suspiciously, she lost her job, was kidnapped, beaten, raped, and escaped after reporting to police.

propositions.text: Panel determines claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection for stated reasons.
propositions.quote: The panel determines that the claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection" for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The panel determines the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Panel cannot establish nexus between claimant's fear and grounds in section 96; will analyze under subsection 97(1).
propositions.quote: The panel cannot establish a nexus between the fear of persecution raised by the claimant and one of the five grounds set out in section 96 of the Act. Accordingly, the panel will conduct its analysis under subsection 97(1) of the Act.

paragraphs.summary: The panel cannot establish a nexus to section 96 grounds and will analyze under subsection 97(1).

propositions.text: Claimant's identity established by passport issued by Ukrainian authorities filed by Immigration services.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity has been established to the panel's satisfaction by means of a copy of her passport, which was issued by the Ukrainian authorities and filed as evidence by Immigration services.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's identity established by Ukrainian passport evidence.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation for delay in visa application is not accepted; undermines subjective fear of risk.
propositions.quote: The panel does not accept this explanation because the time between when the claimant alleged that her life was at risk... was very long... This undermines the claimant's subjective fear.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects claimant's explanation for visa delay, undermining her subjective fear.

propositions.text: Claimant's inconsistent date about meeting with organized crime leader undermines credibility.
propositions.quote: This response leaves the panel confused because this information was discussed a few minutes earlier... This undermines the claimant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's inconsistent date about meeting undermines credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant's inconsistent statements about date of boss's death undermine credibility.
propositions.quote: The claimant then stated that it must have been XXXX XXXX XXXX 2008... claimant stated that she did not know whether it was Saturday or Sunday...

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's inconsistent statements about boss's death date undermine credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant's failure to produce original newspaper excerpt leads to negative inference about genuineness.
propositions.quote: The panel does not accept this explanation and draws a negative inference from the fact that the claimant did not produce the original newspaper...

paragraphs.summary: The panel draws negative inference from claimant's failure to produce original newspaper, doubting genuineness.

propositions.text: Date on newspaper excerpt was not translated; panel requested translation and received it as P-16.
propositions.quote: The panel therefore requested that this date be translated and gave a deadline to have this done. The panel received the requested translation and listed this document as P-16.

propositions.text: Date on newspaper (P-16) is earlier than death date, claimant's explanation rejected; document not genuine and no probative value.
propositions.quote: How could people have issued condolences in a newspaper dated XXXX XXXX XXXX 2008, if the person died only on XXXX XXXX, 2008?... The panel does not accept this explanation... It is reasonable to believe... This document is not genuine. Therefore, it attaches no probative value to this document.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the newspaper date inconsistent with death date, rejects claimant's explanation, and finds document not genuine.

propositions.text: Claimant's inconsistent testimony about kidnapping and questioning undermines credibility; panel doubts her story.
propositions.quote: The panel does not accept this explanation and is of the opinion that the claimant is attempting to adjust her testimony... All of this is inconsistent...

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's inconsistent testimony about kidnapping undermines credibility and doubts her story.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation why kidnappers wanted bank documents despite her no longer working there is not accepted; panel does not believe kidnapping occurred.
propositions.quote: The panel does not accept this explanation. All of this is inconsistent, and the panel does not believe that the claimant was kidnapped or detained.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects claimant's explanation about kidnappers' motives and does not believe kidnapping occurred.

propositions.text: Claimant says organized crime still searches for her but not her parents; panel finds this unlikely given parents' address is official.
propositions.quote: The panel does not believe that these people would still be searching for the claimant without looking for her at parents' home...

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds it unlikely organized crime searches for claimant but not her parents at their official address.

propositions.text: Panel does not believe claimant's story of being sought by organized crime; attaches no probative value to several documents including medical certificates and police responses.
propositions.quote: For all these reasons, the panel does not believe the claimant's story... the panel attaches no probative value to documents P-8 and P-9... P-10 through P-12...

propositions.text: Documentary evidence indicates fraudulent medical and police reports are possible in Ukraine due to low salaries and corruption.
propositions.quote: documentary evidence indicates that "it is possible to obtain fraudulent medical and police reports throughout Ukraine" because "police officials and hospital staff in Ukraine earn a low salary and some are therefore willing to accept money to produce such fraudulent documents."

propositions.text: Panel found document P-13 not genuine.
propositions.quote: The panel has already found that the document submitted by the claimant under P-13 was not a genuine document.

paragraphs.summary: The panel disbelieves claimant's story, attaches no value to documents, notes evidence of fraud in Ukraine, and found P-13 not genuine.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant's testimony not credible and she failed to prove serious possibility of persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if returned.
propositions.quote: the panel is of the opinion that the claimant's testimony is not credible and that she did not discharge her burden of establishing that there is a serious possibility of her being persecuted on a Convention ground...

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes claimant's testimony is not credible and she failed to prove risk of persecution or harm if returned.

propositions.text: Panel determines claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection and rejects her refugee claim.
propositions.quote: the panel therefore determines that XXXX XXXX is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection. Consequently, the panel rejects her claim for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The panel determines claimant is not a refugee or person in need of protection and rejects her claim.
